**Finding submitted — deviation (T4C), preferred-level cure.**

- **What the document says:** The term is evergreen (§2, p0011) and the only no-cause exit (§6(a), p0032) is gated on there being "no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding." §6(b) is cause-based only, and §3 contains no early-termination or wind-down fee.
- **Why it fails:** We have no convenience right during an active engagement and no prepaid-fee refund — failing both the preferred and the fallback Customer elements.
- **Cure:** One inserted §6(c) giving Company only a right to terminate the Agreement or any SOW on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Unrelated text untouched; no Vendor-side right expanded.
- **Element 4 already met:** §6(a)'s gating means Contractor cannot terminate for convenience while a SOW is outstanding. The 15-day notice in the shell (no-SOW) period is noted in the rationale but not redlined, as no selected element reaches it.
